skills.name: diagnose-pdf
skills.desc: This skill should be used when a PDF made with bidi2pdf (CLI, Ruby API or bidi2pdf-rails) is blank, half empty, unstyled, missing images or fonts, cut off, on the wrong number of pages, shows dates in the wrong format, or breaks words badly. A checklist from the cheapest check to the most expensive, using bidi2pdf diagnose.
skills.body:
---
name: diagnose-pdf
description: This skill should be used when a PDF made with bidi2pdf (CLI, Ruby API or bidi2pdf-rails) is blank, half empty, unstyled, missing images or fonts, cut off, on the wrong number of pages, shows dates in the wrong format, or breaks words badly. A checklist from the cheapest check to the most expensive, using bidi2pdf diagnose.
---

# Find out why a PDF looks wrong

Start with what Chrome reports, not with the page's code. Each check below names what to look at
and the usual cause.

**Does not:** fix the page's design or CSS for you - it finds why the PDF differs from what was
expected, then the fix belongs in the page or the render call.

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. Ask Chrome

```bash
bidi2pdf diagnose --url https://example.com/report --json --screenshot seen.png --pdf try.pdf
```

Use the same `--remote-browser-url`, cookies, headers and waits as the real render: a diagnosis of a
different request explains nothing. Read the JSON in this order.

## 2. The checklist

1. **`network_failures`** - every stylesheet, font, image or script the browser could not load.
   The most common cause of a blank or unstyled PDF: the address works from your machine but not
   **from the browser's**. A browser in a container resolves names in its own network; `localhost`
   there is the container itself. Use an address the browser can reach (for a Rails app, the asset
   host the browser sees - bidi2pdf-rails' asset-host setting), then diagnose again.
2. **`console`** - a script error can stop the page before it renders its content.
3. **`page.url` / `navigation.final_url`** - a redirect to a login page answers 200 and prints
   perfectly; the right cookies or headers are missing. (A 4xx/5xx answer fails the render with
   `NAVIGATION_NOT_FOUND` or `NAVIGATION_FAILED` instead.)
4. **`fonts.status`** - `loading` or entries in `fonts.failed`: the PDF falls back to another font
   or shows boxes. Add a wait (`--wait-network-idle`), or fix the font URL (see 1).
5. **`print_media`** - the page's `@media print` rules and `@page` rules. A print stylesheet that
   hides content, `fixed_or_sticky_elements` repeated on every page, or a `@page` size that fights
   `--page-width`. To print what the screen shows instead: `--media screen`.
6. **`paged_js`** - `detected: true` but `ready: false`: Paged.js had not finished. Render with
   `--wait-window-loaded` and let the page set `window.loaded = true` when Paged.js is done; without
   that flag the wait runs into `--default-timeout`.
7. **Late content** (charts, lazy images): `--wait-network-idle`, or a recipe with `wait_for`
   (`selector:` of the last thing that appears).
8. **Page count or cut-off content** - page size and margins are in **cm**; Chrome's own default
   margin is 1 cm a side. A layout breakpoint follows the width **between the side margins**, not
   the paper's (96 / 2.54 CSS px per cm).
9. **Dates and number formats** in form fields come from the browser's locale, not the page: set
   `LANG`/`LANGUAGE` on the browser's container (e.g. `de_DE.UTF-8`).
10. **Hyphenation** (`hyphens: auto` does nothing, or breaks anywhere): the browser needs Chrome's
    hyphenation dictionaries installed for the page's `lang`. bidi2pdf's chromedriver image ships
    them; a self-built image may not. The page needs a correct `lang` attribute.

## 3. When the log is needed

`render ... --log-network-traffic --log-level debug` logs every request with its timing.
`--network-log-format pdf` writes that log as its own PDF next to the output. Use it only when the
JSON above did not explain the problem; it is long.

skills.name: page-screenshots
skills.desc: This skill should be used when pages of a web site or app need screenshots for a design, UX or accessibility review - at phone and desktop width, in light and dark mode - or when one screenshot shows what Chrome rendered for a PDF. Uses bidi2pdf's browser (local or a shared chromedriver), not Playwright or Puppeteer.
skills.body:
---
name: page-screenshots
description: This skill should be used when pages of a web site or app need screenshots for a design, UX or accessibility review - at phone and desktop width, in light and dark mode - or when one screenshot shows what Chrome rendered for a PDF. Uses bidi2pdf's browser (local or a shared chromedriver), not Playwright or Puppeteer.
---

# Screenshots for review with bidi2pdf

A reviewer, human or agent, judges a page from what Chrome draws. Shoot every page that changed at
phone width first, then desktop, each in light and dark mode, and hand over the files with the
page and the width in their names.

**Does not:** compare screenshots against a baseline or judge them - it produces them. For a
visual regression check, diff the PNGs in your own test (bidi2pdf's `contains_pdf_image` compares
images inside a PDF, see `pdf-specs`).

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. One shot

```bash
bidi2pdf diagnose --url http://app:4000/pricing --screenshot pricing.png --media screen --color_scheme dark
```

The shot is the whole document at the browser's default viewport. Good for "what did Chrome see";
for review sets with fixed widths use the script below.

## 2. A review set

```bash
SKILL_DIR=/absolute/path/to/skills/page-screenshots
ruby "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/screenshots.rb" --base http://app:4000 --pages /,/pricing,/signup \
  --widths 360,1280 --out tmp/screenshots --remote-browser-url http://remote-chrome:3000/session
```

Set `SKILL_DIR` first, to the absolute path of this skill's own folder - the folder of this SKILL.md, which the
agent (Claude Code, Codex) names when it loads the skill. Nothing guarantees that the variable is already set:
without it, the command looks for `/scripts/screenshots.rb`. In a checkout of bidi2pdf it is
`"$PWD/claude-plugin/skills/page-screenshots"`. Run the script by that path, not relative to the project you are
shooting.

It writes one PNG for every page, width and colour scheme and prints each path:
`<page path>-<width>-<scheme>.png`, with the page's folders kept (`/account/settings` becomes
`account/settings-360-light.png`, `/` becomes `index-...`). When a page's path holds characters a file
name should not, or a query, the name gets a short hash of the path, so no two pages overwrite each
other. It sets the viewport, emulates `prefers-color-scheme`
with `media: screen`, waits for the network to go quiet and captures the full page. Without
`--remote-browser-url` it starts a local chromedriver. It needs the bidi2pdf release with
`BrowserTab#emulate_media` (0.1.23 or later).

- **360 px first.** Most layout bugs show at the narrow width; 1280 covers desktop. Add the site's own
  breakpoints when they matter (e.g. 768).
- **The base URL is seen from the browser.** A shared browser in a container cannot reach
  `localhost` on your machine - use a name it resolves.
- A page that needs a login: open it in the Ruby API with a cookie (`tab.set_cookie`) before
  navigating, or shoot a page that does not need one.

## 3. From Ruby

The same steps for your own test or tool:

```ruby
tab.emulate_media(media: "screen", color_scheme: "dark")
tab.set_viewport(width: 360, height: 900)
tab.navigate_to("http://app:4000/pricing")
tab.wait_until_network_idle
tab.screenshot("tmp/pricing-360-dark.png")
```

`screenshot(origin: "viewport")` captures exactly the viewport instead of the whole page. A full-page
shot is as wide as the document, not the viewport: a page laid out by Paged.js comes out at its sheet
width (794 px for A4) once Paged.js has finished - a print layout, not a 360 px one. A
page that toggles dark mode by a class or `data-theme` instead of `prefers-color-scheme` needs that
attribute set (`tab.execute_script(...)`) - emulation changes only the media feature.

## 4. Hand-over

List the files with page, width and scheme, and say what the reviewer should look at (the changed
part). Reviewers need both widths and both schemes; a dark-mode contrast bug never shows in a light
screenshot.

skills.name: pdf-recipe
skills.desc: This skill should be used when a PDF needs more than one render call - waiting for an element, clicking something open, running a script, switching to screen view or a viewport first - or when a PDF must be checked (page count, text in it, no failed requests). Writes and validates a bidi2pdf recipe YAML without a browser, then runs it.
skills.body:
---
name: pdf-recipe
description: This skill should be used when a PDF needs more than one render call - waiting for an element, clicking something open, running a script, switching to screen view or a viewport first - or when a PDF must be checked (page count, text in it, no failed requests). Writes and validates a bidi2pdf recipe YAML without a browser, then runs it.
---

# Write and run a bidi2pdf recipe

A recipe is a rendering contract: the steps a page needs before it is printed, and what the PDF must
be like afterwards. It is not a general automation script. The source of truth for its shape is
`bidi2pdf schema recipe`; read it once before writing one.

**Does not:** log in through forms, follow links across pages, or extract data. One page, prepared
and printed. For a plain page without steps, `render` is enough (the `render-pdf` skill).

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. Write it

```yaml
version: 1
source:
  url: https://example.com/invoice/123
actions:
  - wait_for:
      selector: "#invoice"
      timeout: 10
  - click:
      selector: "#show-details"
  - wait_network_idle:
      timeout: 10
assert:
  - selector_exists:
      selector: "#total"
  - no_console_errors: true
  - page_count: 2
  - pdf_text_present:
      text: "Invoice #123"
output:
  pdf: invoice.pdf
  manifest: invoice.manifest.json
```

- **source**: exactly one of `url`, `file`, `stdin`.
- **actions** run in order, **after** the page has loaded:
  - `wait_for` takes exactly one of `selector`, `paged_js: true` (a Paged.js page exists) or `script`
    (a JS expression that becomes truthy), plus an optional `timeout` (default 10 s).
  - `click`, `evaluate` (a script, optionally `assign:` its result), `inject_script`/`inject_style`
    (`content:` or `url:`).
  - `set_viewport` (`width`, `height`, optional `device_pixel_ratio`).
  - `wait_network_idle` (`timeout`).
  - `emulate_media` (`media: screen|print`, `color_scheme: light|dark`, `reduced_motion`) - from the
    0.1.23 or later.
- **assert** runs after printing. Page checks: `selector_exists`, `text_present`,
  `no_console_errors`, `no_network_failures`, `fonts_loaded`. PDF checks: `page_count`,
  `pdf_text_present`, `pdf_not_blank` - these need the `pdf-reader` gem.
- **output** needs at least one of `pdf`, `manifest`, `screenshot`.

Two rules people trip over:

- `no_console_errors`, `no_network_failures`, `fonts_loaded` and `pdf_not_blank` are presence-only:
  write them as `true`. `false` is rejected - leave the assertion out instead.
- `no_network_failures` fails on **any** failed request, a missing favicon or a 404 image included.
  Check `bidi2pdf diagnose --json` first and fix the page, or leave that assertion out.

## 2. Validate without a browser

```bash
bidi2pdf run invoice.yml --validate --json
```

This checks the shape, every action and assertion name and every value, and that `pdf-reader` is
there when a PDF assertion needs it - no browser starts. Iterate until `ok` is true; on failure
`error.details.path` names the step (`assert[0].no_console_errors`).

## 3. Run it

```bash
bidi2pdf run invoice.yml --json --remote-browser-url http://chrome:3000/session
```

The result lists every action and assertion with its own `ok`. A failed step stops the run with
`error.code` `PAGE_NOT_AS_EXPECTED` (or `SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND` for a `wait_for` that never matched),
exit code 4, and `error.details` says which check failed and why (for `no_network_failures` the
failed requests). Exit 2 is a recipe the validator refused; exit 3 is the browser or the page not
loading. `--json-stream` reports progress on stderr while it runs.

skills.name: pdf-specs
skills.desc: This skill should be used when writing or fixing RSpec specs that render PDFs or drive pages with bidi2pdf - asserting text, page count or images in a generated PDF, starting a Chrome container for the suite, or a browser spec that is flaky, times out or sees an empty page.
skills.body:
---
name: pdf-specs
description: This skill should be used when writing or fixing RSpec specs that render PDFs or drive pages with bidi2pdf - asserting text, page count or images in a generated PDF, starting a Chrome container for the suite, or a browser spec that is flaky, times out or sees an empty page.
---

# RSpec specs with bidi2pdf's test helpers

bidi2pdf ships RSpec matchers for PDFs and helpers that start a chromedriver container for the
suite. This skill is how to use them, and the mistakes that made such specs flaky before.

**Does not:** replace a project's own spec conventions - follow those for naming and layout. And it
does not cover bidi2pdf-rails' own test helpers (see that gem).

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. Set up

```ruby
# spec/spec_helper.rb
require "bidi2pdf/test_helpers"             # matchers and file helpers; needs pdf-reader, diff-lcs, unicode_utils
require "bidi2pdf/test_helpers/images"      # only for contains_pdf_image (ruby-vips, dhash-vips)
require "bidi2pdf/test_helpers/testcontainers" # only to start Chrome in Docker for the suite
```

# Run a shared Chrome for bidi2pdf

bidi2pdf talks to chromedriver over HTTP and WebDriver BiDi. A chromedriver container that several
processes share is cheaper and more predictable than a browser per process, and keeps Chrome out of
the application's own container.

**Does not:** cover Kubernetes or a cloud browser service, and does not make an untrusted page safe
on its own (section 5 is what it takes).

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. The container

`references/compose.remote-chrome.yml` is a working Compose service, taken from an application that
runs it in development and production. The parts that matter, and why:

- **Image** `dieters877565/chromedriver` (chromedriver + Chromium, hyphenation dictionaries
  included). It answers on port 3000; the new-session URL is `http://<service>:3000/session`.
- **No published port, an internal network only.** Whoever reaches port 3000 drives a browser: keep
  it to the containers that render. No VNC (`ENABLE_VNC: "false"`).
- **Chrome's sandbox** needs to create namespaces, which Docker's default seccomp profile only allows
  with `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. Three ways, from the narrowest:
  1. The gem's seccomp profile `docker/chrome-driver/chrome.json` (`security_opt:
     ["seccomp=chrome.json"]`), no extra capability. It allows the namespace calls Chrome uses, but
     also some Docker's default refuses (`mount`, `bpf`, `ptrace`, `perf_event_open`); verify on your
     host that sessions start before relying on it.
  2. `cap_add: [SYS_ADMIN]` - works with the default profile, and is what the reference file uses. It
     is a broad capability: keep the container on its internal network and give it nothing else.
  3. No extra capability, and every client passes `--no-sandbox` (`DISABLE_CHROME_SANDBOX=true` for the
     CLI). Chrome then runs every page without its own sandbox - only for pages you trust. Some CI
     runners drop `--cap-add` silently; there only this works.
- **Limits from measurement, not guesses:** one Chrome session runs ~110 threads (Docker counts them
  as pids) and a few hundred MB. `pids_limit: 1024`, `mem_limit: 2g` with `memswap_limit` equal (no
  swap: a Chrome out of memory is killed and replaced instead of freezing every render),
  `shm_size: 256m`. At 512 pids and 1 GB, four concurrent renders crashed or froze it.
- **`WATCHDOG_ENABLED: "true"`** stops chromedriver when it stops answering or memory thrashes;
  `restart: unless-stopped` then starts a fresh container. The image's health check (`/status`)
  only marks it unhealthy - Docker never restarts an unhealthy container by itself.
- **`LANG`/`LANGUAGE`** set the browser's locale: date and number formats in form fields follow it.

In CI, wait for the container to be healthy before the first render; "Connection refused" on port
3000 right after start means it was not ready yet.

## 2. Connect

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url http://app:3000/report --output report.pdf \
  --remote-browser-url http://remote-chrome:3000/session
```

The page URL must be reachable **from the browser container**, not from where the command runs:
`localhost` there is the browser itself. Use the application's service name, and for a Rails app
make the PDF's asset host that same name, or every stylesheet fails and the PDF is blank.

## 3. Keep sessions from piling up

A process that crashes or is killed mid-render leaves its Chrome session open on the shared
chromedriver, and each one holds memory. bidi2pdf records the sessions it opens on this machine
(`SessionRegistry`); look and clean up with:

```bash
bidi2pdf sessions --remote-browser-url http://remote-chrome:3000/session
bidi2pdf sweep --remote-browser-url http://remote-chrome:3000/session --dry-run
bidi2pdf sweep --remote-browser-url http://remote-chrome:3000/session
```

`sweep` closes recorded sessions older than `--older-than` (600 s), unresponsive ones, and the oldest
above `--max-sessions`; never one younger than `--min-age` or one a running process holds. Leave
`--scope all` to a chromedriver your application owns alone - it also closes sessions other
programs opened. Run `sweep` from cron or a timer, and `--dry-run` first.

Code that opens its own sessions (a test driver, a script) passes a `SessionRegistry` to
`Bidi2pdf::Bidi::Session.new(..., registry: Bidi2pdf::SessionRegistry.new(url))` and closes the
session in an `ensure`, with a time limit on the close: a hung close is the most common leak.

## 4. Size it

Renders run in parallel on one chromedriver, one session (or a tab of one) each. Measure your own
pages: start with 2 GB, run the peak number of renders at once, and watch `docker stats` for memory
and pids. Raise `mem_limit` and `pids_limit` together.

## 5. Printing HTML nobody vouches for

A page from a user is a page that runs its scripts in your browser. Before navigating:

- `tab.disable_script_execution` - the page's JavaScript does not run at all.
- Give the browser container **no direct internet access**: route it through an egress proxy that
  refuses private and internal addresses, so a page cannot make the browser fetch your internal
  services. Never put it on the same network as your database.
- Prefer printing HTML you built (`render_html_content`, `--html-file`) over handing Chrome a URL a
  user typed.

**Before production, test the isolation with hostile pages**, not by reading the configuration. Render
pages that try, each on its own: to fetch an internal service and your cloud metadata address, to load
`file:///etc/passwd` and other `file:` URLs, to open new windows, to run scripts despite
`disable_script_execution`, and to exhaust memory. Each must fail or stay contained, and the
chromedriver must keep serving other renders. Repeat it after changing the image, the capabilities or
the seccomp profile.

skills.desc: This skill should be used when a web page, a URL or an HTML file has to become a PDF with bidi2pdf's command line, including a PDF of a page's screen view, dark mode or mobile layout, a tagged (accessible) PDF, or a PDF piped through stdin/stdout. Covers the order of commands, the waits, reading the JSON result and the exit codes.

name: render-pdf
description: This skill should be used when a web page, a URL or an HTML file has to become a PDF with bidi2pdf's command line, including a PDF of a page's screen view, dark mode or mobile layout, a tagged (accessible) PDF, or a PDF piped through stdin/stdout. Covers the order of commands, the waits, reading the JSON result and the exit codes.
---

# Render a PDF with the bidi2pdf CLI

bidi2pdf prints a page in a real Chrome over WebDriver BiDi. This skill is the order of work and the
pitfalls; the exact options are in `bidi2pdf help render`, the exact result shape in
`bidi2pdf schema render`. Read those instead of guessing an option.

**Does not:** scrape page content or automate a site (log in, click through). bidi2pdf is a
renderer; for a page that needs steps before printing, write a recipe (the `pdf-recipe` skill).

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. Preflight

```bash
bidi2pdf version --json
```

One call answers three questions: is bidi2pdf there at all, which version (`bidi2pdf`), and whether
`pages` will be filled (`pdf_reader` is `null` without that gem). `--media`, `--color_scheme` and
`--reduced_motion`, and a clean stdout for `--json` and `--output -`, need 0.1.23 or later. If
`bidi2pdf help render` does not list an option, the installed gem is older - say so instead of
working around it.

**When bidi2pdf is missing**, look first, install nothing yet, and suggest the lightest way that fits:

```bash
ruby -v; docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}'; command -v chromium chromium-browser google-chrome
```

1. **Docker answers** (`docker info` prints a server version, not an error - an installed client
   without a reachable daemon or socket permission does not count): nothing to install, the image
   has Ruby, Chromium and pdf-reader. Inside a container that uses the host's Docker, `-v` mounts
   a path of the host, not of the container.
2. **Ruby 3.4 or later is there:** `gem install bidi2pdf`, plus a browser if none was found.
   `pdf-reader` only when the page count is needed.
3. **No Ruby, or an older one:** a distribution's Ruby is too old (Debian 12 ships 3.1, Debian 13
   3.3, Ubuntu 24.04 3.2 - and a `node` image is Debian). Homebrew's `ruby` on macOS, a version
   manager (`mise`, `rbenv`) elsewhere - or option 1, which needs no Ruby at all.

```bash
# 1. Docker: no install
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/reports" dieters877565/bidi2pdf:main-slim \
  bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output /reports/example.pdf --json
# 2. Ruby 3.4+
gem install bidi2pdf
gem install pdf-reader    # optional: fills "pages"
# Browser on Debian, or in a Debian-based container (the packaged driver also works on ARM)
sudo apt-get install -y chromium chromium-driver
# Ruby on macOS (Google Chrome, if installed, is the browser)
brew install ruby
```

bidi2pdf fetches a matching chromedriver itself, which may fail on ARM Linux - there use the
packaged `chromium-driver`. Ubuntu's `chromium` is a snap that does not run in a container: use a
shared browser there (the `remote-chrome` skill).

**Show the user the commands that fit and run them only after a yes** - they change the system.

Where Chrome runs:

- **A shared browser** (a chromedriver container): pass `--remote-browser-url
  http://<host>:3000/session` to every command. The `remote-chrome` skill sets one up.
- **Local**: bidi2pdf starts chromedriver itself; Chrome or Chromium must be installed. Inside a
  container add `--no-sandbox` (or set `DISABLE_CHROME_SANDBOX=true`).

## 2. Render

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com/invoice/123 --output invoice.pdf \
  --wait-network-idle --json --manifest invoice.manifest.json
```

- **Waits.** Without one, bidi2pdf prints as soon as the page's load event fired.
  `--wait-network-idle` waits for late requests (lazy images, fetched data).
  `--wait-window-loaded` waits until the page's **own script** sets `window.loaded = true` - use it
  for Paged.js or any page that finishes rendering itself, never for a page that does not set it:
  that one waits the whole `--default-timeout` (60 s) and fails with `COMMAND_TIMEOUT`.
- **Input.** `--url`, `--html-file`, or `--stdin` for HTML on standard input - exactly one.
- **Output.** `--output file.pdf`; `--output -` writes the PDF bytes to stdout and nothing else (it
  cannot be combined with `--json`).
- **`--manifest`** records what was rendered with which options, to reproduce or debug it later
  (cookie values and secret headers are left out).
- **Cookies, headers, basic auth:** `--cookie name=value`, `--header Name=value`, `--auth user:pass`.

```bash
cat page.html | bidi2pdf render --stdin --output - > page.pdf
```

## 3. Page size, margins, screen view, mobile layout

All sizes are **centimetres**: `--page-width`/`--page-height` (default US Letter, 21.59 x 27.94),
`--margin-top/-bottom/-left/-right`. Chrome's own default margin is 1 cm a side.

By default Chrome prints with the page's **print stylesheet**. To print what the screen shows:

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output screen.pdf --media screen
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output dark.pdf --media screen --color_scheme dark
```

A **mobile layout** needs a narrow page. A printed page is laid out between its side margins, at
96 / 2.54 = about 37.8 CSS px per cm, so set the side margins yourself:

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output phone.pdf --media screen \
  --page-width 9.525 --page-height 20 --margin-left 0 --margin-right 0
```

9.525 cm without side margins is 360 px; 8.467 cm is 320 px. With Chrome's default 1 cm margins a
9.5 cm page is only about 283 px wide and may hit a smaller breakpoint than intended.

For an accessible PDF add `--generate-tagged-pdf` (and `--generate-document-outline` for bookmarks).

## 4. Read the result, not the logs

With `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON document; logs go to stderr. Check `ok`, then:

- `pages`, `bytes`, `sha256` of the PDF. `pages` is `null` without `pdf-reader`, with a warning:
  report it that way, or ask before installing that gem - no other PDF tool for a page count.
- `navigation.final_url` - a redirect to a login page answers 200 and prints perfectly. (A status
  of 400 or more fails the render instead.)
- `network_failures` and `console` even when `ok` is true: a missing image still gives a PDF.
- On failure `error.code`, `error.retryable` and `error.hint`. Retry only when `retryable` is true.

The exit code says the same without parsing:

| Code | Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_PRINT_OPTION` | 2 | an option value bidi2pdf refuses - fix the command |
| `MISSING_INPUT` | 2 | none of --url, --html-file, --stdin given |
| `DNS_ERROR` | 3 | the host does not resolve **from the browser's machine** |
| `NAVIGATION_TIMEOUT` | 3 | the page did not load in time |
| `NAVIGATION_NOT_FOUND` | 3 | the URL answered 404 |
| `NAVIGATION_FAILED` | 3 | the URL answered another 4xx/5xx, or the connection failed |
| `BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED` | 3 | no Chrome/chromedriver - see section 1 |
| `COMMAND_TIMEOUT` | 3 | a wait never finished (often `--wait-window-loaded`) |
| `PDF_GENERATION_FAILED` | 6 | Chrome could not print |
| `OUTPUT_WRITE_FAILED` | 6 | the output path cannot be written |

The full list: `bidi2pdf schema render` (the `error` object) and README "Exit codes".

`--json-stream` writes one progress event per line to stderr while it runs (`bidi2pdf schema
event`), for a long render a user should see move.

## 5. When it fails or looks wrong

Only then, with the same options as the render:

```bash
bidi2pdf diagnose --url https://example.com/invoice/123 --json --screenshot seen.png
```

`diagnose` loads the page like `render` and prints no PDF; `console`, `network_failures`,

skills.bodyMd:
# Render a PDF with the bidi2pdf CLI

bidi2pdf prints a page in a real Chrome over WebDriver BiDi. This skill is the order of work and the
pitfalls; the exact options are in `bidi2pdf help render`, the exact result shape in
`bidi2pdf schema render`. Read those instead of guessing an option.

**Does not:** scrape page content or automate a site (log in, click through). bidi2pdf is a
renderer; for a page that needs steps before printing, write a recipe (the `pdf-recipe` skill).

## Ground rules

- **bidi2pdf is the renderer.** If it fails, report its `error.code`, `error.hint` and exit code;
  never make the PDF or screenshot another way (Chrome's own print-to-PDF, another PDF engine).
- **Install nothing unasked.** Name what is missing and suggest a way (the `render-pdf` skill's
  preflight); run nothing that changes the system without the user's yes.
- **bidi2pdf's results first.** Read its `--json` result instead of inspecting the PDF with other
  tools.

## 1. Preflight

```bash
bidi2pdf version --json
```

One call answers three questions: is bidi2pdf there at all, which version (`bidi2pdf`), and whether
`pages` will be filled (`pdf_reader` is `null` without that gem). `--media`, `--color_scheme` and
`--reduced_motion`, and a clean stdout for `--json` and `--output -`, need 0.1.23 or later. If
`bidi2pdf help render` does not list an option, the installed gem is older - say so instead of
working around it.

**When bidi2pdf is missing**, look first, install nothing yet, and suggest the lightest way that fits:

```bash
ruby -v; docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}'; command -v chromium chromium-browser google-chrome
```

1. **Docker answers** (`docker info` prints a server version, not an error - an installed client
   without a reachable daemon or socket permission does not count): nothing to install, the image
   has Ruby, Chromium and pdf-reader. Inside a container that uses the host's Docker, `-v` mounts
   a path of the host, not of the container.
2. **Ruby 3.4 or later is there:** `gem install bidi2pdf`, plus a browser if none was found.
   `pdf-reader` only when the page count is needed.
3. **No Ruby, or an older one:** a distribution's Ruby is too old (Debian 12 ships 3.1, Debian 13
   3.3, Ubuntu 24.04 3.2 - and a `node` image is Debian). Homebrew's `ruby` on macOS, a version
   manager (`mise`, `rbenv`) elsewhere - or option 1, which needs no Ruby at all.

```bash
# 1. Docker: no install
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/reports" dieters877565/bidi2pdf:main-slim \
  bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output /reports/example.pdf --json
# 2. Ruby 3.4+
gem install bidi2pdf
gem install pdf-reader    # optional: fills "pages"
# Browser on Debian, or in a Debian-based container (the packaged driver also works on ARM)
sudo apt-get install -y chromium chromium-driver
# Ruby on macOS (Google Chrome, if installed, is the browser)
brew install ruby
```

bidi2pdf fetches a matching chromedriver itself, which may fail on ARM Linux - there use the
packaged `chromium-driver`. Ubuntu's `chromium` is a snap that does not run in a container: use a
shared browser there (the `remote-chrome` skill).

**Show the user the commands that fit and run them only after a yes** - they change the system.

Where Chrome runs:

- **A shared browser** (a chromedriver container): pass `--remote-browser-url
  http://<host>:3000/session` to every command. The `remote-chrome` skill sets one up.
- **Local**: bidi2pdf starts chromedriver itself; Chrome or Chromium must be installed. Inside a
  container add `--no-sandbox` (or set `DISABLE_CHROME_SANDBOX=true`).

## 2. Render

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com/invoice/123 --output invoice.pdf \
  --wait-network-idle --json --manifest invoice.manifest.json
```

- **Waits.** Without one, bidi2pdf prints as soon as the page's load event fired.
  `--wait-network-idle` waits for late requests (lazy images, fetched data).
  `--wait-window-loaded` waits until the page's **own script** sets `window.loaded = true` - use it
  for Paged.js or any page that finishes rendering itself, never for a page that does not set it:
  that one waits the whole `--default-timeout` (60 s) and fails with `COMMAND_TIMEOUT`.
- **Input.** `--url`, `--html-file`, or `--stdin` for HTML on standard input - exactly one.
- **Output.** `--output file.pdf`; `--output -` writes the PDF bytes to stdout and nothing else (it
  cannot be combined with `--json`).
- **`--manifest`** records what was rendered with which options, to reproduce or debug it later
  (cookie values and secret headers are left out).
- **Cookies, headers, basic auth:** `--cookie name=value`, `--header Name=value`, `--auth user:pass`.

```bash
cat page.html | bidi2pdf render --stdin --output - > page.pdf
```

## 3. Page size, margins, screen view, mobile layout

All sizes are **centimetres**: `--page-width`/`--page-height` (default US Letter, 21.59 x 27.94),
`--margin-top/-bottom/-left/-right`. Chrome's own default margin is 1 cm a side.

By default Chrome prints with the page's **print stylesheet**. To print what the screen shows:

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output screen.pdf --media screen
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output dark.pdf --media screen --color_scheme dark
```

A **mobile layout** needs a narrow page. A printed page is laid out between its side margins, at
96 / 2.54 = about 37.8 CSS px per cm, so set the side margins yourself:

```bash
bidi2pdf render --url https://example.com --output phone.pdf --media screen \
  --page-width 9.525 --page-height 20 --margin-left 0 --margin-right 0
```

9.525 cm without side margins is 360 px; 8.467 cm is 320 px. With Chrome's default 1 cm margins a
9.5 cm page is only about 283 px wide and may hit a smaller breakpoint than intended.

For an accessible PDF add `--generate-tagged-pdf` (and `--generate-document-outline` for bookmarks).

## 4. Read the result, not the logs

With `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON document; logs go to stderr. Check `ok`, then:

- `pages`, `bytes`, `sha256` of the PDF. `pages` is `null` without `pdf-reader`, with a warning:
  report it that way, or ask before installing that gem - no other PDF tool for a page count.
- `navigation.final_url` - a redirect to a login page answers 200 and prints perfectly. (A status
  of 400 or more fails the render instead.)
- `network_failures` and `console` even when `ok` is true: a missing image still gives a PDF.
- On failure `error.code`, `error.retryable` and `error.hint`. Retry only when `retryable` is true.

The exit code says the same without parsing:

| Code | Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_PRINT_OPTION` | 2 | an option value bidi2pdf refuses - fix the command |
| `MISSING_INPUT` | 2 | none of --url, --html-file, --stdin given |
| `DNS_ERROR` | 3 | the host does not resolve **from the browser's machine** |
| `NAVIGATION_TIMEOUT` | 3 | the page did not load in time |
| `NAVIGATION_NOT_FOUND` | 3 | the URL answered 404 |
| `NAVIGATION_FAILED` | 3 | the URL answered another 4xx/5xx, or the connection failed |
| `BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED` | 3 | no Chrome/chromedriver - see section 1 |
| `COMMAND_TIMEOUT` | 3 | a wait never finished (often `--wait-window-loaded`) |
| `PDF_GENERATION_FAILED` | 6 | Chrome could not print |
| `OUTPUT_WRITE_FAILED` | 6 | the output path cannot be written |

The full list: `bidi2pdf schema render` (the `error` object) and README "Exit codes".

`--json-stream` writes one progress event per line to stderr while it runs (`bidi2pdf schema
event`), for a long render a user should see move.

## 5. When it fails or looks wrong

Only then, with the same options as the render:

```bash
bidi2pdf diagnose --url https://example.com/invoice/123 --json --screenshot seen.png
```

`diagnose` loads the page like `render` and prints no PDF; `console`, `network_failures`,
`fonts.status`, `print_media` and `paged_js` usually name the cause. The checklist: the
`diagnose-pdf` skill.
